system.biography:
Background

Embraced in 1467, Parovich witnessed the fall of a New York prince to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} and became convinced the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} will inevitably win the Jyhad against a divided, squabbling @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}. Decades ago he secretly contacted the Sabbat and was initiated into the Black Hand, and he now sits on the Council of Milwaukee as its @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} representative while quietly working to undermine the city from within: encouraging Elder-Anarch infighting, corrupting the Anubi's effectiveness against the Lupine, and Blood Binding as many Kindred as possible in preparation for a Sabbat takeover. Several of his own childer — including Anastasia and their self-appointed leader Kristian — discovered his Sabbat ties and fled into hiding rather than be Blood Bound to his cause; Parovich has already killed two of them and hunts the rest.

Roleplaying Hints

Play Parovich as unfailingly kind, forgiving, and understanding no matter the provocation — the better to make his eventual betrayal land harder. Never openly vindictive.
system.notes: Sire: Boronisk. Childer: Anastasia, Kristian, and at least two more (two already killed by Parovich for fleeing). Haven: a condemned house in the Barrens that he keeps from being demolished through bureaucratic influence. Masks his stench in Council with an overly sweet perfume. Disciplines as printed: Animalism 5, Celerity 1, Obfuscate 4, Potence 4, Thaumaturgy 1 (capped above to this system's 1-5 scale).

items.name: Animalism — 4 Elder — Song in the Dark

system.description: Loremasters tell of vast, atavistic creatures that tunnel and crawl beneath the earth, older than the clan's flight into the sewers. Only Nosferatu methuselahs are said to be potent enough to draw on this power, summoning and commanding such a creature once each year for every five Willpower Traits they possess; the vampire must burn these temporary Traits for at least one month before regaining them. The size of the resulting subterranean disturbance depends on a Charisma- and Survival-related challenge, with difficulty set by how rural the chosen location is (an uninhabited stretch of desert is easy; downtown Manhattan is nearly impossible). This power is Storyteller-adjudicated: she may forgo game mechanics entirely and simply narrate the consequences (a sinkhole, a collapsed tunnel, a distant earthquake) rather than resolve it as a formal challenge.
system.source: Clanbook: Nosferatu, Chapter Two: Inside Clan Nosferatu
system.bloodCost: 5 Willpower Traits per use (burned for one month)

system.description: While many Kindred find the blood of animals revolting, you are able to reap unique benefits from this type of feeding. This power doubles the number of Blood Traits you may obtain from any single animal you feed from. It is not in effect when you feed on humans.

Reaches into a target's self-image and lets the Malkavian assume the appearance and false memories of whoever has most shaped (or damaged) that self-image — a sire, a parent, a priest, or whoever the target's own psyche supplies.

MET System: Win a Social Challenge against the victim. On a win, you gain a free retest on your very next use of Dementation, Dominate, or Presence against that same victim. Once the retest is used, the power's knowledge fades unless you spend a Willpower Trait to keep it active for one further retest (this is expensive, but more certain than triggering the power again from scratch). You may only claim one retest per challenge this way. This power relies heavily on the target's own good-faith roleplaying — if the subject's player won't cooperate, don't force it with a Storyteller ruling.

By spending a Mental Trait per subject, you extend any Obfuscate power you possess over a group, hiding or disguising them collectively; the cloak fails entirely only if you yourself are noticed or violate your power's conditions.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description:
Facetiously named, this power allows the Kindred to physically knock another character away from herself with the slightest of touches. Although this power does no damage in and of itself, its use is quite humbling — to be hurled away from an elder in a social setting has its embarrassing repercussions. Some Kindred use this power surreptitiously, touching their victims and sending them reeling across the room; others use it as a not-so-subtle display of their might, giving their victim a casual slap with overwhelming results.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait and must succeed in a physical challenge to touch the target (this may be done surreptitiously, but the player may not make use of other Potence benefits). The challenge is not required if the subject allows the player to touch him (a handshake, a “friendly” hand on the shoulder, etc). This power hurls the victim 20 feet directly away from the invoking character. If the subject strikes a wall or other solid obstacle, he suffers two health levels of bashing damage. Otherwise, the character needs to win a static physical challenge against six Traits to remain standing.
By spending a Blood Trait, you gain one additional action at the end of the turn, after all basic actions resolve.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines
